provenance.method: Each method read in full against the definitions in plan/04_STRUCTURAL_LABELS.md. Two judgements per property: the definitional one (does the property hold as written, with the plan's fixed vocabularies) and the semantic one (does it hold in the code's actual behaviour).
provenance.unord_rule: P_UNORD was judged to hold only when a value *produced by iterating* an unordered collection -- a for-each/iterator element, a keySet/entrySet/values traversal, or a rendering of the whole collection whose result depends on its order -- reaches an assertion argument. A collection merely passed to an opaque call does not qualify.
provenance.development_pass: An earlier pass over a different 50-method sample surfaced four analyser bugs (timed Thread.join not treated as a barrier; verify(mock).start() counted as a dispatch; map.get(k) results carrying collection taint; try-with-resources initialisers never analysed). Those were fixed before this audit was scored. The P_UNORD tightening below was driven by false positives in THIS sample, so the P_UNORD precision reported here is optimistic and is flagged as such.
provenance.keyed_by: uid (sha1 of the normalised code). FlakeBench's `id` collides between its flaky and non-flaky halves, so ids 335 and 361 were disambiguated by the project of the method actually read.
